# Focused Std solver-session cost diagnostic

This workflow reuses `std-first-compilers-dev` from public run `37248167583`; it builds no compiler. Source pins remain original `97601b75712f458de37a13bf9953a0b7825122eb`, repaired `b615831aaa26fea72364627d0fe6040f10e49eee` and final `a5304cd9aeb5e4fd12700aa2e61125a904d58996`. Every original input/plan and both actual archived compiler component identities are checked before and after measurement.

The three matched jobs select only the affected TargetSpecific-cs / Z3 5.1.0, TargetSpecific-notarget / Z3 5.1.0, and TargetSpecific-notarget / Z3 4.16.0 parts. Each job runs three paired samples with the original cores 4 arguments and two separately labeled cores 1 controls, sequentially on its host. Arm starts alternate and rotate across jobs; an odd count of three cannot balance each job perfectly. There are nine canonical pairs plus six additional controls, thirty invocations in total. No seeds, original resource limits, canonical declaration order or original source options change. Both compilers omit extended-newtype-bases and AdditionalAxioms. The runner retains the existing process/job safety caps and reports incomplete samples.

The sole added observation option is the existing `--solver-log`. Every checker-suffixed log is retained with raw hashes. The pure SMT parser records exact token/command byte ranges, command hashes, emitted `:boogie-vc-id` lexical tokens, assertion hashes and complete preceding-session hashes. It neither executes nor rewrites, normalizes or sorts SMT commands. It does not invent VC/batch identities when markers are absent. A marker segment can include pop/reset/new background commands for the next query; the raw complete session remains authoritative. Missing, empty or malformed logs leave query observation incomplete. Files above the parser's 256 MiB safety cap remain raw evidence with unavailable parsed metadata.

Actual verifier exits, stdout/stderr, warning lines, declaration/batch outcomes and RU, BPL and session logs are preserved. Setup/build-receipt/extraction failures block proof execution and produce metadata. Unexpected runner failure or absent summaries produces an explicit incomplete runner state. Each workflow step retains a diagnostic exit 0 and the aggregate always labels `report: false`; this is deliberate evidence collection, not an Actions success claim. The aggregate's separate exactness/completeness fields report observed facts. Controls never substitute for the canonical cores 4 requirement, and no expected tables are updated.

Byte-identical translated BPL precedes engine VC construction and does not prove actual solver-query or reusable-session equality. Repeated same-compiler variation, logged session history and the labeled cores 1 controls help distinguish scheduling/reuse effects from consistent arm-specific changes. Any RU movement, semantic log difference, warning or missing observation remains unresolved until reviewed.

Pure preparation checks: `diagnose_cost.py check` validates generated options and bounded sample plans; `solver_sessions.py check` tests exact SMT token ranges and malformed/unsupported cases. Those modes invoke no compiler or solver. `diagnose_cost.py aggregate` reads retained artifacts only.
